Great to meet you both last week. This thread is a short operational kickoff to confirm the CS <> Implementation handoff for Meditech's quality monitoring (prompt sets, eval harness integration, regression alerts, and canary/rollback controls). Goal: have the first canary live in staging by 2026-06-01 and production rollback policy agreed by 2026-06-10.

Initial asks for this week:
- Meditech: confirm the initial prompt set owner (who will own prompt edits in the first two sprints)
- RW team: deliver the eval harness integration checklist and a sample promptset CSV by EOD Wed 2026-05-20
- Security/Compliance: note that we will need the sandbox audit logs for the first canary window (2 weeks)

I've attached a starter promptset and a proposed canary/fallback matrix. Marissa, can you take point on the eval harness checklist? Lauren, can you draft the rollback SLA language we propose for the account?

Thanks —

Thanks — two quick notes from product/clinical:
- We do need clinician vs patient prompt variants. I'll upload a CSV with ~40 prompts across both personas by Friday.
- For canary thresholds: our tolerance window for false positives in clinical assistance is very low — if the regression detects >0.5% critical-safety divergence (per promptset sampling) we want an automatic pause and a rollback to the last verified model variant. Is that something you can automate, or do we need runbook steps?

Tom

Meditech Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

On Mon, 2026-05-18 Tom Reyes wrote:
> For canary thresholds: our tolerance window for false positives in clinical assistance is very low — if the regression detects >0.5% critical-safety divergence (per promptset sampling) we want an automatic pause and a rollback to the last verified model variant. Is that something you can automate, or do we need runbook steps?

Tom — we can do both. Proposed approach:
- Primary: automated pause + rollback when the eval harness flags a critical-safety regression above the agreed threshold (0.5% in your note). Redwood can wire a webhook from the eval pipeline to trigger a canary pause and immediate fallback to pinned model variant.
- Secondary: a manual runbook with step-by-step rollback (for audit trails) and a 30-minute on-call window during the first two canary weeks.

Draft rollback SLA language (summary):
- Automatic rollback will be executed within 90s of a verified critical-safety regression alert from the eval pipeline.
- Post-rollback, we will open a postmortem within 48 hours and supply tokenized request/response samples for debugging (redacted).
- Meditech will have read-only access to the canary audit stream for the two-week window.

I'll push a short doc with the exact webhook schema and a sample Postman collection to the Drive link in this thread by EOD. Monica — can you sign off on the on-call commitments for the first two weeks?

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Product Manager, Installations
Redwood Inference
